title: The thing with feathers
hookLine: hope is the thing with feathers that perches in the soul
tomorrow: who comes in a carriage to take Dickinson for a ride?

cards: Some people tape a line to the bathroom mirror, words to get through the week.
Emily Dickinson, writing in her family's house in Amherst, gave hope a body instead. ""Hope" is the thing with feathers That perches in the soul." Not a plan. Not a mood.
A bird, small, landed inside, singing.

teach.b: Look at what the bird does. It "sings the tune without the words, And never stops at all." No words: it can't argue anyone out of anything.
It just keeps singing. Dickinson says it sounds sweetest in the gale, and she's heard it in the chillest land and on the strangest sea.
Then the last turn: never, even at the worst, did it ask a crumb of her. That's the teaching. In Dickinson, hope isn't something you manufacture or earn.
You don't even feed it. It perches on its own and asks nothing. Your part is to notice it's still singing.
Now, a look back, because it's review day.

teach.h: TWO POETS, BOTH LISTENING FOR BIRDS.
teach.b: I celebrate myself, where every atom is shared. What is the grass, and an honest I don't know. I contain multitudes.
In perfect silence, under the stars.
Lilac and star and bird, grief with something to hold. And the visitor at the bedside. Whitman sang out loud, for everybody, in the street.
Dickinson sings small, in a quiet room. Both, it turns out, listen for birds.

how: Some readers of Dickinson learn this short poem by heart and say its first lines on hard days; some keep a small bird, a feather or a picture of one as a reminder.

games.q: what does “the thing with feathers” mean?
o: a bonnet Dickinson wore out in her garden
a quill pen Dickinson used to write poems
Dickinson's name for hope: a bird in the soul

games.q: a bird called hope: tap the pairs.
p: what it never asked of her

s: Dickinson's hope talks you out of despair with words
it sings the tune without the words.
in the poem, hope never asked a crumb of her

games.q: a friend's job search keeps failing, and someone tells her to 'manifest harder.' what fits Dickinson's poem?
o: hope isn't something you produce; it perches on its own, and you can listen for it.
hope works if you feed it enough positive words every day.
hope is a reward that shows up once things go right.
games.why: Dickinson's bird sings without words and asks nothing. hope isn't a performance to keep up; it's a song to notice.

practice: Sit, and listen for the smallest steady sound near you: a bird outside, the fridge, your own breath. Don't decide what it means. Just let it keep going, the way Dickinson's bird never stops at all.

wordCard.voice: The thing with feathers: Dickinson's name for hope, a small bird that perches in the soul, sings without words and never asks a crumb.

carryVoice: For the road: the thing with feathers. It asks nothing of you; it perches, and it sings. Till next time.
